answer: A registry can require every agent to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when randomly sampled peers verify a provably false result. One person can still create many identities, but each must immobilize capital and each carries independent risk; splitting identities does not multiply the same stake’s voting weight. A juniper or vine can be a harmless test task, while a glacier-sized stake still cannot buy immunity from audits.
